newsitem.title: USA: Hilton says confident it can acquire ITT.
newsitem.headline: Hilton says confident it can acquire ITT.

text.p: Hilton Hotels Corp Chief Executive Officer Stephen Bollenbach said the company is on track in its $6.5 billion hostile bid to acquire ITT Corp and is confident it can complete a deal.

"Our offer to acquire ITT...represents another unique opportunity for the shareholders of both companies, and we are on track for what we are confident will be a successful conclusion," Bollenbach said in a statement.
Earlier, Hilton reported first quarter earnings of $0.26 a share on revenue of $1.3 billion in the first quarter versus $0.19 a share on revenue of $957 million last year.
Analysts had expected Hilton, the largest hotel and gambling company in the United States, to earn $0.23 a share in the first quarter, according to research firm First Call.
Hilton shares were up 1-1/8 to 26-7/8 by midday.

Hilton attributed the strong earnings report to its $3.0 billion acquisition of gambling company Bally Entertainment Corp in 1996 and its purchase of six upscale, full service hotels from Prudential Insurance Co of America.
But gaming operations were affected by flooding in Reno, Nev., and by soft market conditions in Laughlin, Nev., Tunica, Miss., and Kansas City.

The Bally acquisition added new hotel/casinos in Las Vegas, Atlantic City, Mississippi and New Orleans. Gaming division earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA) rose to $133 million from $54 million.

At the Las Vegas Hilton, high-rolling baccarat card games saw a win percentage of 27 percent, which was normal versus an abnormally low rate last year. EBITDA, also called cash flow, at the hotel improved to $19 million from $1.0 million.
Overall occupancy at hotels in the gaming division, however, declined 1.5 points to 87.2 percent with the average daily room rate increasing four percent to $77.38.
